status.en: 214 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Plateau State.
status.nb: 214 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Plateau State.

summary.en: Gunmen continue to target civilians and security forces across Plateau and Zamfara, killing vigilantes, miners, a traditional ruler, and police officers in separate attacks. In Plateau, bandits killed four vigilantes and two miners, while gunmen shot the MACBAN chairman and the Miyetti Allah chairman, wounding them. In Zamfara, gunmen killed three police officers during a night patrol and three more in a separate patrol attack. Islamic State claimed responsibility for a deadly strike on a military camp. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Skytevåpen fortsetter å ramme sivile og sikkerhetsstyrker i Plateau og Zamfara, og dreper voktere, gruvearbeidere, en tradisjonell leder og politifolk i separate angrep. I Plateau drepte banditter fire voktere og to gruvearbeidere, mens skytevåpnene skjøt MACBAN-lederen og Miyetti-Allah-lederen, og såret dem. I Zamfara drepte skytevåpnene tre politifolk under en natts patrulje og tre til i et eget patruljeangrep. IS tok ansvar for et dødelig angrep på en militærleir. Konflikten førte til 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
